capabilities: Sync tagged reMarkable notebooks, PDFs and EPUBs into vault folders as Markdown notes
Transcribe handwriting to searchable text using local or cloud backends
Extract PDF highlights and margin notes as quote digests with stable block IDs
Send Zotero PDFs to the tablet and write highlights back to Zotero as annotations
Push highlights and margin notes to Readwise
disambiguation: Not a two-way vault sync; it is a one-way import from the reMarkable tablet and never writes to the device.
extras: Freemium: the free tier covers sync, local transcription and PDF digests; Pro (EUR 24 once, no subscription) adds multi-tag sync, direct-from-tablet sync, cloud transcription, Zotero write-back and Readwise push, with a 14-day trial. Desktop only; Obsidian mobile is unsupported. The reverse-engineered reMarkable cloud API can break on firmware changes, which the README discusses at length.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to get handwritten notebooks and PDF markups off a reMarkable tablet into the vault as searchable, linkable notes.

relations.evidence: the plugin authenticates to my.remarkable.com via a one-time device code
Your reMarkable highlights land in Zotero as native annotations.
Your reMarkable highlights land in your Readwise library as ordinary highlights
Install and start Ollama, LM Studio, or any other server that speaks the OpenAI
The default on macOS 13 or later, and nothing to configure.

requires.name: Zotero API key, Readwise token, or cloud transcription API key
Tagged Sync Pro licence (EUR 24 one-time) and a Readwise API plan

summary: One-way sync that imports tagged reMarkable notebooks, annotated PDFs and EPUBs into the vault as Markdown with page renders, transcribed handwriting and highlight digests.
